small_guidance:
- Drop the per-(N, OH-tile, OW-tile) atomic_add accumulator: launch grid as (N, cdiv(OW, BLOCK_W)) and have each program loop over OH internally so the partial sum is reduced in registers and stored once — eliminates atomics and redundant weight reloads across OH tiles.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_W (256) and try BLOCK_OH that covers the full OH in one program (persistent over OH); also sweep num_warps=8 with num_stages=3 since the inner GEMM is BLOCK_OC×BLOCK_IC = 128×64 which is sizable.
- Reorder loops so the kh/kw static loops are outermost and the OH loop is inside; this lets `w_tile` be loaded once per (kh,kw) and reused across all OH rows in the tile, cutting weight bandwidth by ~BLOCK_OH×.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a gather-style direct conv-transpose where each program owns one (n, ow-tile) column and walks the full OH dimension internally, accumulating min-then-sum in registers; this removes the atomic_add reduction across OH tiles entirely and fuses the H-sum into the kernel cleanly.
- Use an im2col-GEMM formulation in channels_last layout: K dim = IC*KH*KW, M dim = OC, N dim = OW (per row of OH per batch). Inside the kernel, for each oh row, compute the OC×OW conv tile via tl.dot, take min over OC, accumulate into a per-(n,ow) register vector across oh, then epilogue GELU+bias and store. One launch, no atomics.
- Consider precomputing in the launcher a dense (OC, IC, KH, KW) → (IC*KH*KW, OC) reordered weight (channels-last K-major) to make the inner GEMM contiguous; this is a layout transform of the existing weight (no axis collapse) and improves load coalescing for the K-reduction.
